description:
The Croydon Urban Room is a space to talk about the past, present and future of the Croydon town centre. Through conversa­tions, stories, exhibitions and events, the Urban Room brings together the views of those who live, work and visit the area to create a shared vision of the future and test new uses live in action. 

See our website for further details of specific events.

factsheet.heading: Collaborative City
paragraphs: Drop-in for a workshop during Open House to re-imagine our town centre. We will be interacting with our scale model, replacing already existing buildings with ones you might want to see.

factsheet.heading: Nicolette Duckham: Look Up Croydon
paragraphs:
Croydon council's lead conservation officer, Nicolette Duckham, will be taking us on a walking tour of North End, encouraging us to 'look up'! 
We will meet at the Croydon Urban Room:  Sunday 13th September 14:00 - 15:30.

factsheet.heading: Insitu: Illuminating Croydon
paragraphs: Join us for a free creative workshop exploring North End and Wellesley Road, and the role they play within the wider journey of Croydon town centre.

Using a large illuminated map, participants will choose a section of the town centre and add their ideas, dreams and aspirations through drawing and collage. Together, we'll create a glowing lantern of local voices and visions, showcasing what our town centre could become.

factsheet.heading: Becky Lyon: Mapping the Town Centre
paragraphs: We invite Croydon locals for a playful, creative workshop exploring the possibilities of North End and Wellesley Road — how could could we brighten and enrich the Croydon town centre experience. Co-hosted by the Croydon Urban Room and Croydon-born artist, researcher and London National Park City Ranger Becky Lyon, we’ll explore how we feel about these places today and what we want them to become.

factsheet.heading: The Glass House: Town Centre Futures
paragraphs: What if young people could use gaming to help express their ideas about the spaces they would like to have in real life?

Join us for a free, full-day workshop for children aged 10 to 13 and their parents/guardians, where you will explore the Future of the High Street thinking about the past, present and future, in collaboration with national charity The Glass-House Community Led Design.

factsheet.heading: Russell Royer: Clubs of the Future
paragraphs: As part of Croydon Urban Room's ongoing window exhibition series and Open House, Russell Royer will be leading a workshop celebrating the social clubs of Croydon. We will be engaging with the exhibition itself and understanding what kinds of clubs exist already in Croydon. We'll then discuss what could come next. Always wanted to start a chess club? Think Croydon is missing a knitting group? Today might be the day you start one!
